primary_driver: Direct U.S.-Iran combat is widening through attacks on Gulf energy infrastructure, shipping routes, and Iranian-aligned forces, while Russia's war against Ukraine continues to generate spillover risk into NATO airspace.
primary_stabilizer: Active diplomatic and support channels remain open through NATO, the Ukraine Defence Contact Group, presidential travel, and UN nuclear-monitoring mechanisms, although none has yet produced durable de-escalation.

headlines.title: U.S.-Iran fighting keeps oil above $100 as Strait of Hormuz traffic remains severely disrupted
headlines.summary: AP reports that renewed U.S.-Iran attacks are constraining energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, with major implications for global prices, shipping, and allied economic resilience. The combination of direct combat and energy disruption raises systemic spillover risk.

headlines.title: IAEA board refers Iran to the UN Security Council
headlines.summary: The referral represents a significant deterioration in the nuclear-diplomatic track and increases the risk of sanctions, countermeasures, and further military escalation. Russia and China may limit punitive action, but the procedural breakdown is strategically destabilizing.

headlines.title: Yemen risks renewed civil war as Iran-backed forces threaten Gulf shipping alternatives
headlines.summary: Iran-linked Houthi activity is tying the Yemen conflict more closely to the U.S.-Iran war and to the security of Red Sea and Gulf trade routes. This creates an additional escalation pathway involving Saudi Arabia, the United States, and regional proxy forces.

headlines.title: Zelenskyy seeks further military support in Canada as Russian drone attacks continue
headlines.summary: Ukraine is pursuing additional external military backing while Russian strikes continue, including a deadly attack in the Kyiv region. The war remains active at high intensity and continues to draw NATO states deeper into sustained material support.

headlines.title: Drone incursion disrupts Zelenskyy's flight and crosses into NATO-member Romania
headlines.summary: A suspected Russian-type drone incident involving Moldovan and Romanian airspace demonstrates continuing spillover risk from the Ukraine war. The event did not trigger direct NATO-Russia combat but increases air-defense and alliance-alert pressures.

headlines.title: NATO welcomes new Ukraine-support commitments from allies
headlines.summary: NATO says allies committed additional support, including air-defense assistance and funding through established mechanisms. This strengthens alliance cohesion and Ukrainian resilience but also formalizes continued long-term confrontation with Russia.

areas_to_watch.name: Strait of Hormuz and Gulf energy infrastructure
areas_to_watch.why: Further attacks on tankers, ports, refineries, or naval vessels could convert the existing energy shock into a broader global economic and military crisis.

areas_to_watch.name: Iran-linked proxy expansion
areas_to_watch.why: Houthi, Iraqi militia, Lebanese, Syrian, or other aligned forces could widen the U.S.-Iran conflict across multiple theaters and increase pressure on Gulf states.

areas_to_watch.name: NATO airspace incidents along the eastern flank
areas_to_watch.why: Repeated drone or missile incursions into Romania, Moldova-adjacent airspace, Poland, or the Baltic region could produce a politically difficult demand for direct alliance response.

areas_to_watch.name: Iran nuclear monitoring and retaliation
areas_to_watch.why: The UN Security Council referral, disrupted verification, and continued strikes create incentives for Iran to restrict inspections or accelerate sensitive nuclear activity.

areas_to_watch.name: Ukraine support and Russian escalation
areas_to_watch.why: Additional Western air-defense and long-range-strike support may improve Ukraine's position but could also prompt intensified Russian attacks on cities, logistics, or NATO-linked infrastructure.

areas_to_watch.name: Diplomatic channel durability
areas_to_watch.why: NATO, UN, and Ukraine-related diplomatic mechanisms remain active, but their failure to produce ceasefires or enforceable restraint would push the diplomatic-breakdown factor higher.

methodology.note: Analytical early-warning index, not a probability forecast.
methodology.formula: Weighted average of ten 0–10 factor scores, multiplied by 10 and rounded.
